proofs.boundary_clarification: For k>1, if card(x)=1 then f(x)=1>=1/k directly. Otherwise choose i with 0<x_i<1 and define v=(x-x_i e_i)/(1-x_i); then v is in Delta_n, v_i=0 and card(v)=card(x)-1<=k-1. This clarification is supplied locally, not quoted as explicit original wording. The scalar identity is (1-beta)^2/(k-1)+beta^2 = 1/k + k/(k-1)*(beta-1/k)^2.
proofs.locator: Registered supplementary PDF page 12, Appendix C, Lemma’ 3; statement also on page 5, Lemma 3
map: The original proof inducts on the support budget k. The base case is a simplex vertex, whose squared norm is one.
It writes x=(1-gamma)v+gamma e_i with gamma=x_i, v_i=0 and card(v)<=k-1; orthogonality gives f(x)=(1-gamma)^2 f(v)+gamma^2.
The induction hypothesis bounds this below by (1-gamma)^2/(k-1)+gamma^2. Minimizing over gamma in [0,1] gives 1/k.
The equality paragraph constructs k coordinates equal to 1/k.

proofs.full_local_argument: Fix arbitrary integers n>=1 and 1<=s<=n, and arbitrary x in Delta_n with card(x)<=s. Set S=supp(x) and m=|S|. Since sum_i x_i=1, S is nonempty and 1<=m<=s. Cauchy-Schwarz applied to (x_i)_{i in S} and the all-ones vector in R^m yields 1=(sum_{i in S} x_i)^2 <= m sum_{i in S} x_i^2=m f(x). Thus f(x)>=1/m>=1/s. Equality f(x)=1/s forces both inequalities to be equalities: m=s and all coordinates on S equal; their sum one forces each to be 1/s. Conversely, any subset S of size s exists because s<=n, and the vector equal to 1/s on S and zero elsewhere belongs to Delta_n, has card(x)=s and f(x)=s*(1/s)^2=1/s. This proves the exact minimum and all equality cases. Every simplex vector has at most n nonzero coordinates, so applying the proved statement with s=n gives the unrestricted simplex minimum 1/n, whose equality characterization forces every coordinate to be 1/n and hence gives a unique minimizer. Subtracting this minimum from the pointwise inequality gives f(x)-min_{Delta_n} f>=1/s-1/n with the same equality cases. For n=s=1 the simplex consists of (1), and every formula holds. No division by zero occurs because m,s,n are positive.

assumptions: n is an integer with n>=1.
The feasible outputs are exactly x in Delta_n with card(x)<=s; the norm is the Euclidean norm.
statement.conclusion: min_{x in Delta_n, card(x)<=s} ||x||_2^2 = 1/s. Equality holds if and only if x has exactly s nonzero coordinates, each equal to 1/s. Taking s=n gives min_{x in Delta_n} ||x||_2^2=1/n, uniquely at x*=(1/n,...,1/n). Consequently every feasible support-constrained x has f(x)-f(x*)>=1/s-1/n, with equality at the same uniform-on-s-coordinate vectors. This includes n=s=1.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For n coordinates, Delta_n = {x in R^n: x_i>=0 for every i in {1,...,n}, sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1}. Define supp(x)={i:x_i!=0}, card(x)=|supp(x)|, and f(x)=||x||_2^2=sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2=x^T x. Let e_i be the standard coordinate vectors.
statement.parameter_domains: n in Z, n>=1; s in Z, 1<=s<=n. The paper's support-budget symbol k is renamed s here.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such integer pair (n,s), every x in Delta_n with card(x)<=s satisfies f(x)>=1/s. For every subset S of {1,...,n} with |S|=s, the vector with coordinates 1/s on S and zero elsewhere attains equality. The claim is deterministic and pointwise, with no oracle or algorithm assumptions.

summary: For integers n>=1 and 1<=s<=n, the minimum of ||x||_2^2 over probability-simplex vectors with at most s nonzero coordinates is exactly 1/s. This is a sparsity restriction.
title: Minimum Euclidean squared norm under a simplex support constraint
